suggested_text.VII_D_e_latex: \emph{(e) LLM raters without further human labeling} (post hoc, no new human label; Supplementary Section~S28). Two experiments asked whether LLM-rater labels behave like a measuring instrument. The rater prompt of Supplementary Section~S21 (the human raters' criteria) and a deterministic check that the cited span occurs verbatim in the rendering were applied to the $182$ primary cells that have a subgraph view. The S21 rater, \texttt{gpt-5.6-luna}, could not be run again (its quota was exhausted), so an open-weight rater, GLM-4.7-Flash, took its place. Two temperature-$0$ runs started $35$ minutes apart agreed closely (Krippendorff $\alpha=0.91$ $[0.77,0.98]$ on support, QWK $0.92$), which measures serving determinism only. Three runs at temperature $0.7$ did not ($\alpha=0.21$), and two reworded prompts moved the labels ($\alpha=0.60$ together with the original wording). The unsupported-credit estimate $\hat\pi$ ranged over $22$ percentage points across the seven runs ($38\%$ to $60\%$). Across families (GLM-4.7-Flash and gpt-oss-20b; no Anthropic model could be reached) the agreement on support was $\kappa=0.20$ $[0.04,0.36]$, and each rater's $\kappa$ with the AH labels and with the second rater lay between $-0.06$ and $0.16$, against $\kappa_{\mathrm{source}}=0.595$ between the two human raters (margin $0.10$, so a lower bound of at least $0.495$ was required; the human-human interval $[0.268,0.833]$ is wide). The LLM raters marked $19$ to $36\%$ of cells as supported against $67.0$ and $73.4\%$ for the two humans, and a rater from the extractor's own family (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) did not differ detectably from the cross-family raters in $\kappa$ with the humans (difference $+0.03$ $[-0.13,0.14]$). Rerunning the audit unchanged on a majority vote of three LLM raters (GLM-4.7-Flash, gpt-oss-20b and the S21 labels) gives $\hat\pi=45.7\%$ $[33.9,58.0]$, and gate G1 still fails. None of this measures accuracy: the criteria for stability and for human-level agreement were not met, so LLM-rater labels remain a sensitivity analysis and not a substitute for human labels.
